probe.note: Five neutral probe solves (weighted sum, no floors) of the actual design problem; values are achieved, feasible designs. Ranges are indicative, not exhaustive.

justification.normalisation: Runtime bounds follow the physical ~41 to ~62 h envelope stated for this case, siren spans the probe range (2.1 to 3.14 h) up to the 3 h requirement, voice uses the stated ~70 to 90 SII band, and L5 uses the stated ~0.05 to 0.30 feasible band, so no objective is scaled to favour another.
justification.scalarisation: Achievement (Tchebycheff) is chosen because the probe set shows a non-convex runtime/siren/L5 trade-off (e.g. the L5 probe drops runtime to 45 h while the siren probe gives 3.14 h), which a weighted sum cannot reach.
justification.aspiration: Runtime 62 h and siren 3.1 h are each within the probe-achieved maxima (62.28 h and 3.14 h), voice 78 and L5 0.27 are only marginally above the best probes (77.7 and 0.267), so all aspirations are reachable or nearly so.
justification.objective_floors: The brief states emergency endurance of at least 3 hours as a requirement, and the siren probe shows 3.14 h is feasible alongside about 62 h runtime, so a 3.0 h floor is achievable; runtime (~60 h) is marketing language, not a requirement, so it stays a goal rather than a floor.
justification.weights: Runtime and siren carry the most weight because they are the two stated hard-program outcomes (60 h battery and 3 h siren), L5 is weighted equally with siren since 'strong GNSS L5' is a stated program goal and is the lowest-achieved objective (0.073 to 0.267), and voice is weighted slightly lower because its probe spread is narrow (74.6 to 77.7).

justification.scalarisation: Achievement (Tchebycheff) is retained because the probes show a non-convex runtime/siren/L5 trade-off (the L5 probe gives 0.267 L5 but drops runtime to 45.2 h, while the siren probe gives 3.14 h), which a weighted sum cannot reach.
justification.aspiration: Siren aspiration is raised from 3.1 to 3.14 h because the siren probe achieves 3.141 h, and at that same design runtime is 62.03 h, so runtime 62 and siren 3.14 are jointly reachable; voice 78 and L5 0.27 sit just above the best probes (77.7 and 0.267) and are reachable or nearly so.
justification.objective_floors: The brief and the program direction make endurance of at least 3 h of the 86 dB @ 1 m siren a hard requirement, and the siren probe shows 3.14 h is feasible, so the 3.0 h floor is kept as a hard constraint; runtime stays a goal because the ~60 h figure is marketing language rather than a requirement, and 86 dB @ 1 m is enforced through the arbiter's acoustic response targets rather than as an objective.
justification.weights: Siren weight is raised from 0.25 to 0.40 because the program direction makes the siren the safety-critical feature, runtime is reduced to 0.25 because it is a marketing goal and its aspiration is already met by the siren-probe design, L5 is kept at 0.20 as a stated program goal with the lowest achieved values (0.073 to 0.267), and voice is reduced to 0.15 because its probe spread is narrow (74.6 to 77.7).

justification.scalarisation: Achievement (Tchebycheff) is kept because the probes show a non-convex trade-off: the L5-best probe gives 0.267 but only 45.2 h runtime and 2.10 h siren, which a weighted sum cannot reach at any balance.
justification.aspiration: L5 0.27 is set at the best probe (0.267) because L5 is now the top program priority and needs to be pushed as far as the feasible set allows; runtime 62 h and siren 3.1 h are within the probe maxima (62.28 h, 3.14 h); voice 78 is just above the best probe (77.7), so all aspirations are reachable or nearly so.
justification.objective_floors: The brief states at least 3 hours of emergency siren endurance as a requirement, and the siren probe shows 3.14 h is feasible, so the 3.0 h floor is hard and achievable; ~60 h runtime is marketing language, not a requirement, so it stays a goal, and no L5 floor is imposed because the brief defines L5 as a goal to maximise.
justification.weights: Program direction says outdoor athletes and GNSS L5 are the top priority, so L5 is raised to 0.40, the largest weight, and runtime (0.25) stays above siren (0.20) because the siren floor already guarantees the 3 h requirement; voice is lowest (0.15) because its probe spread is narrow (74.6 to 77.7) and it is not a stated requirement.

justification.scalarisation: Achievement (Tchebycheff) is kept because the probes show a non-convex runtime/siren/L5 trade-off (the L5 probe gives 45.2 h runtime while the siren probe gives 3.14 h), which a weighted sum cannot reach, and voice-first priority is better expressed as a shortfall target than as a linear sum.
justification.aspiration: Voice 78 is only 0.3 above the best probe (77.7), runtime 62 and siren 3.1 sit inside the probe maxima (62.3 h and 3.14 h), and L5 0.27 is near the best probe (0.267), so every aspiration is reachable or nearly so.

**(1) Concessions versus original claims**
Every domain gave volume back, consistent with the program direction. The largest cuts were V_ant 1500.0

justification.normalisation: Runtime (41 to 62.5 h), siren (2.0 to 3.2 h), voice (70 to 90 SII) and L5 (0.05 to 0.30) span the stated physical envelopes and probe ranges (runtime 45.2 to 62.3, siren 2.10 to 3.14, voice 74.6 to 77.7, L5 0.073 to 0.267), so no objective is scaled to favour another; the baseline is unchanged.
justification.scalarisation: Achievement (Tchebycheff) is kept because the L5 probe (0.267 at 45.2 h) and siren probe (3.14 h at 62.0 h) show a non-convex runtime/L5/siren trade-off that a weighted sum cannot reach.
justification.aspiration: Runtime 62.0 h, siren 3.1 h, voice 78 and L5 0.27 each sit at or just above the best single-probe values (62.28, 3.14, 77.7, 0.267), so each is individually reachable, though runtime and L5 cannot both be achieved at their maxima together (L5 probe gives 45 h), so the point is a utopia target and not a jointly feasible point.
justification.objective_floors: The brief makes the 3 h siren endurance a requirement ('keeps sounding for >= 3 hours'), and the siren probe proves 3.14 h is feasible (with runtime 62.0 h), so the 3.0 h floor is achievable; the ~60 h runtime is marketing language and stays a goal, not a floor.
justification.weights: Runtime (0.30) and siren (0.25) carry the most weight as the two hard program outcomes (60 h battery, 3 h beacon), L5 (0.25) matches siren as a stated program goal and is the lowest-achieved objective, and voice (0.20) is weighted lowest because its probe spread is narrow (74.6 to 77.7).
justification.program_direction: Per the schedule direction, no field was changed from the reviewed baseline: the port and wall stay as the domains allocate them and the arbiter does not reopen their ranges, which avoids re-running the study.

justification.normalisation: Runtime bounds follow the physical ~41 to ~62.5 h envelope, siren spans the probe range (2.1 to 3.14 h) up to the 3 h requirement, voice uses the stated 70 to 90 SII band, and L5 uses the stated 0.05 to 0.30 band, so no objective is scaled to favour another; these bounds are unchanged from baseline because the program direction is a weighting change, not a rescaling.
justification.scalarisation: Achievement (Tchebycheff) is kept because the probes show a non-convex runtime/siren/L5 trade-off (the L5 probe gives 45.2 h and 0.267, the siren probe gives 3.14 h and 0.073), which a weighted sum cannot reach.
justification.aspiration: The siren probe achieves runtime 62.03 h and siren 3.141 h simultaneously, so the runtime 62.0 and siren 3.1 aspirations are jointly reachable; voice 78 and L5 0.27 sit only marginally above the best probes (77.7 and 0.267).
justification.objective_floors: The brief states the 3 h siren endurance as a requirement, and the siren probe shows 3.14 h is feasible, so 3.0 h is a hard floor; runtime (~60 h) is marketing language rather than a requirement, so it stays a weighted goal and is not floored, which avoids over-constraining the interior volume.
justification.weights: Runtime and siren are raised to 0.35 each because the program direction makes them the joint headline specs and the probes show they can be met together (62.3 h with 2.89 h, or 62.0 h with 3.14 h); L5 is held at 0.2 because it is a stated goal but conflicts directly with both headline specs (0.073 to 0.267 across probes); voice drops to 0.1 because the brief gives only a qualitative intelligibility goal and its probe spread is narrow (74.6 to 77.7).

justification.normalisation: Bounds are unchanged from the reviewed baseline because they follow the stated physical runtime envelope (about 41 to 62.5 h), the probe-achieved siren span up to the 3 h requirement, the stated 70 to 90 SII band, and the stated 0.05 to 0.30 L5 band, so no objective is scaled to favour another.
justification.scalarisation: Achievement (Tchebycheff) is kept because the probes show a non-convex runtime/siren/L5 trade-off (the L5 probe gives 0.267 at 2.10 h siren, while the siren probe gives 3.14 h at 0.073 L5), which a weighted sum cannot reach, and the program direction needs the L5 and voice corners reached rather than a compromise midpoint.
justification.aspiration: Voice 78 (probe best 77.7) and runtime 62 (probe best 62.28) are at the probe maxima, siren 3.1 (probe best 3.14) is reachable, and L5 0.27 is only marginally above the best probe (0.267), so every aspiration is reachable or nearly so.
justification.objective_floors: The brief makes the 3 h emergency siren endurance a hard requirement, and the siren probe shows 3.14 h is feasible, so a 3.0 h floor is achievable; the ~60 h runtime is marketing language rather than a requirement, so it remains a goal and not a floor.
justification.weights: Per the program direction (GNSS and voice first), L5 is raised to 0.35 and voice to 0.30, the two connectivity and call outcomes; siren is kept at 0.20 because its 3 h requirement is enforced as a floor; runtime is reduced to 0.15 from the baseline 0.30 because the 60 h figure is a goal, and the L5 probe shows runtime is what gives way to L5 (45.2 h at 0.267).
